doc.title: Mike Wofford interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998

chapter: Singers: Sarah Vaughan and Ella Fitzgerald
title: Recording All That Jazz and becoming Ella's accompanist
summary: He did the sessions after rehearsing with Ella at her house, apparently as a trial set up by Norman Granz, then started touring with her at a lighter schedule.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I see you were part of the “All That Jazz” the Grammy award winner. Did you get a Grammy for that?

No it didn’t. Actually that was the first time I had worked with Ella. I got called to do that session. Actually there were a total of four sessions, I did two of them, Kenny Barron did — I think I did three and Kenny did one or something like that for that CD. And then on the basis — I think as I realized later, I think Norman Granz knew he was going to have to find someone for Ella because Paul Smith was leaving, the accompanist who had been with her. And I think he hired me to do the CD to see how we worked together. Because I did, prior to actually going into the studio I did go to the house a couple of times and Ella and I would work out some things and keys and tempos and so on, and I think that was kind of Norman’s way of seeing what the chemistry was like and if I would be right. And apparently on the basis of how things went he and she felt comfortable. And not too long after we did the recordings for the CD, their office called me to see if I wanted to start doing the touring, which by that time was not that heavy. You know Ella was going out

oh maybe just a few days a month. We might be gone a total of a week out of a month maybe. In her prime, earlier, before she’d had some health problems, I think she was on the road about 50 weeks out of the year, like Sarah. But she had to curtail some of that. Her doctors had forced her to. But we still were out there quite a bit.
